requirement: Each item's attachments appear in source order.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation: each item's attachments appear in source order. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[rust_attachments_keep_the_owner_kind_and_original_bytes]` is the only {test} reference, and it checks that obligation adequately.

- **Test input.** The source has an item (`fn f`) with two identical `/// café` doc comments, then `#[inline]`, then a trailing `// trailing` comment. The test also checks a module-level comment item (`//! file docs`) and an item with no attachments.
- **Interleaving.** `from_legacy` pushes all comments first and then all annotations, so the raw order is comment, comment, trailing comment, annotation. Source order puts the annotation before the trailing comment. The test asserts the exact sequence `[Comment, Comment, Annotation, Comment]` with their source text, so an implementation that did not sort by position would fail it.
- **Identical comments.** The two doc comments have the same text, so the text comparison alone cannot tell them apart. The assertion `items[2].attachments[0].span.end <= items[2].attachments[1].span.start` checks that they appear in span order.
- **Implementation check.** I read `Outline::from_legacy` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs` only to see how attachments are merged. It merges comments and annotations from separate lists and then sorts with `sort_by_key` on the span start. The test therefore exercises the one conditional behavior this requirement covers.

I found no other {impl} or {test} sites for this requirement, and the acknowledgments list is empty, so I found no gap.
